steps.content: The endless shows have left Sallie almost numb. As long as she can stand and walk, she has to dance—even when she's distracted by her worry for Milly.

The eyes below the stage only care about flesh; no one is really watching the dance. When the lights dim, the guests grow restless. Many climb directly onto the stage, grabbing any dancer that catches their eye, man and woman alike.

Out of the corner of her eye, Sallie sees a guest heading toward her. The gleaming black metal mask overlaps with the golden owl mask in her memory. Her stomach lurches, and she almost throws up. But fear roots her to the spot. She can only stand, paralyzed, in the dispersing crowd.
Spacing out when you should be leaving? You got a death wish?!
The sharp rebuke yanks her out of those terrifying, chaotic memories. Snow strides over and grabs her arm.

steps.speaker: Snow
steps.content: If you don't want guests, just get out of here! Don't stand around, are you begging to be picked?! Dense as you are, you'll be dead in this place before you even know it!
She doesn't stop chiding as she yanks Sallie back a few quick steps.

But this time, Sallie doesn't push her away. Perhaps the fight had been worn out of her. Or perhaps... after these few days, she can finally sense the subtle kindness between the wooden, humble dancers.

steps.speaker: Snow
steps.content: Pull yourself together! Milly will come back.
Snow gives Sallie a hard shove, pushing her off the stage.

Sallie's body is still numb. She glances back and sees the magician—who had bullied her, but also helped her—shoot her an exasperated look from the shadows of the stage, before walking with Snow toward that guest.
